articles.title: How the fear of being single alters modern dating choices
articles.summary: Modern dating is intensely affected by cultural pressures. A new study reveals how a deep dread of remaining unpartnered is linked to anxious young men abandoning dating applications, seeking traditional romance, and passing up on risky, casual sex.

articles.title: Machine learning and online tests identify autistic adults with 92% accuracy
articles.summary: Diagnosing autism in adults can be difficult due to long wait times. A new study shows that combining a standard questionnaire with online mental tests and artificial intelligence can predict an autism diagnosis with 92% accuracy.

articles.summary: A new study in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests scary music subtly alters how people interpret facial expressions. By tracking subjective ratings and eye responses, researchers found ominous soundtracks can make even friendly faces feel threatening.

articles.title: Experts say blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
articles.summary: A new report suggests that blood pressure may be controlled more effectively by increasing potassium while also cutting sodium. Potassium-rich foods can help balance sodium’s effects, but most people consume far less potassium than recommended.

articles.title: AI can tell if your brain is aging faster than you are
articles.summary: A person’s sleeping brain may reveal warning signs of dementia long before memory problems begin. Researchers used machine learning to analyze EEG recordings from about 7,000 adults and found that an older-than-expected “brain age” was tied to a sharply higher dementia risk. Every additional 10 years of brain aging raised that risk by nearly 40%.

articles.title: Scientists discover how obesity may fuel Alzheimer’s disease
articles.summary: Researchers have uncovered a possible biological pathway connecting obesity to Alzheimer’s disease. Obesity appears to raise levels of certain fat molecules that can travel to the brain, disrupt its immune defenses, and promote harmful amyloid buildup. Correcting this fat imbalance improved memory and brain function in Alzheimer’s models.
